summary: Paul Nietupski works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure around 1881–1891. He subsequently held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot specialized in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied in Paris under Senart, Lévi, Chavannes, Dordier, and d'Hervey de Saint Denys, later serving at EFEO (1900) and Collège de France (1909; 1911–1945).
Paul Regnaud was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1869 to 1876 and held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at Rennes and the University of Paris. His main academic posts included Strasbourg (1948–1956), Paris Nanterre (1964–1970), the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1956–1980), and Chicago (1970–1985).

Paul Tedesco worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied philology at the University of Vienna (1916–1921), conducted research at Princeton (~1938–1944), and served as a professor at Yale University (1952–1966).

Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and under Kamalakanta Mishra. His academic posts included Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale (1954–1960), and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich worked in religious studies and philosophy. After earning degrees at Halle-Wittenberg and Breslau, he held professorships at Dresden, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard University (1955–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan from circa 1971 to 1976. He served as an associate professor and department chair at the University of Colorado from circa 1985 to 1993.

Paul Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Sussex and Oxford (DPhil) and served on the faculty at the University of Bristol from circa 1980 until 2011 as Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy.

Paul de Lagarde worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied in Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Friedrich Rückert, later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1851–1852) and the University of Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Paula Arai specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at Kalamazoo, Waseda, and Harvard, later holding positions at Vanderbilt University (1994–2002), Louisiana State University (2007), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Collegio San Pancrazio, served on the Malabar Mission (1776–1789), and held posts with the Congregation of the Index and Pontifical Urban University in 1800.

Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as Professor of Pali and principal at the University of Rangoon (1912–1946) and principal of the University of Adult Education (1947).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. She studied at National Taiwan University and UCLA (PhD 2002), where Donald F. McCallum supervised her doctorate alongside teachers Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Pema Bhum specializes in Tibetology. He previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist practitioner and scholar who studied at Sarah Lawrence, UC Berkeley, and under Chögyam Trungpa, among other teachers. She served as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center and held leadership roles at Gampo Abbey.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin was a student who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Loden was a student who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.
